newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to stay in Bosnia only if U.S. stays too.
newsitem.headline: France to stay in Bosnia only if U.S. stays too.

text.p: France will stay in Bosnia as part of an international force to replace the current NATO-led IFOR soldiers only if the United States also keeps troops in such a unit, a top Defence Ministry aide said on Thursday.
"France's position is that...we came with the Americans and we will leave with them. That will remain our position," ministry spokesman Pierre Servent told a news briefing.

Servent, a close aide to minister Charles Millon, was answering questions on a report in the usually well-informed daily Le Monde saying France and its allies already had plans for a new international unit to replace IFOR when its mandate ended at the end of the year.
IFOR's role is to implement the Bosnia peace accord.
The newspaper said the new force would be 15,000 to 20,000 strong instead of IFOR's 60,000 troops and France's own contribution would be whittled down to 2,500 from the current 7,500.
Le Monde said a novelty in the new force would be the inclusion of German combat troops instead of solely logistics and support units such as are now attached to IFOR.
But Servent said: "There is no specific plan. It is obvious that studies are being made ahead of the December (expiration of IFOR's mandate) but we will make no comment about them."

The aide said the matter would be discussed at an informal meeting of North Atlantic Treaty Organisation defence ministers in Bergen, Norway, on September 25-26 but that much depended on the results of Bosnia's forthcoming elections.

Le Monde said plans were for "IFOR-2" to be commanded by U.S. General William Crouch from the Heidelberg, Germany, headquarters of NATO's central European ground forces, assisted by a multinational staff.
